decisions.decision: mechanismRefEquals normalizes an absent layer to default before comparing slot key sets
decisions.why: Not in the task list, but required: a ref stored in a draft before the layer slot existed carries {hostKey,char} while a freshly built one carries {hostKey,char,layer:default}, so raw key-set comparison called them distinct and duplicated the chip on every revisit. Two shipping dedupe/revisit tests caught it. This extends the absent-layer===default compatibility guarantee from the appliers to the studio dedup, keeping {K_A,a-acute,default} and {K_A,A-acute,shift} correctly distinct.
decisions.rejected: Editing the two failing dedupe tests, which would have shipped a real backward-compatibility defect for every stored touch draft

decisions.decision: The proposal carries a hook-derived parallelCombo alongside the source combo
decisions.why: The data model gives the combo variant only the source combo, but the confirm handler needs the case-shifted base/content letter. Deriving it at confirm time would have made a second caseCounterpart caller and broken FR-002s structural guarantee. Deriving it inside propose keeps the hook the sole casing source.
decisions.rejected: Re-deriving the uppercase base letter in the gallery confirm handler

decisions.decision: S-03 proposals ride the existing onApplied callback rather than a second banner in SequenceBuilderPanel
decisions.why: FR-011 requires one affordance across all three mechanisms; MechanismGallery owns the single hook and banner. The panel returns a SequenceApplied payload (absent on a dedup no-op) and the gallery raises the proposal.
decisions.rejected: Giving SequenceBuilderPanel its own useCasePairCompanion instance and banner

decisions.decision: The parallel sequence ref lands in the counterparts own sequence bucket
decisions.why: collapsedChar is the counterpart, and a bucket is keyed by the assignment target, so partitionSequenceAssignment is called with the counterpart. This matches how the physical non-CAPS path appends an assignment targeting the counterpart, and inherits the existing (firstLetterOut, secondLetter) dedup.
decisions.rejected: Appending the parallel ref to the source characters bucket, which would have made collapsedChar disagree with the assignment target

decisions.why: The invariant was encoded three times (both appliers plus TouchGallery normalizeTouchSlots) and now gates case-pair ref equality, so independent drift would silently break dedup. Engine is the right home since studio already depends on it.
decisions.rejected: Leaving three copies, or moving it to contracts (wrong dependency direction)

decisions.decision: Georgian/Cherokee unicameral-script gap documented as an accepted v1 limitation rather than code-fixed
decisions.why: Spec 051 explicitly places any change to the caseCounterpart primitive out of scope, and propose-then-confirm means nothing is auto-inserted. Recorded in spec Edge Cases, Assumptions, Out of scope, and the casePair.ts docstring so it is a known gap rather than a surprise.
decisions.rejected: Adding a script-aware suppression list, which would have meant changing the frozen primitive

The physical alreadyProduced predicate builds a RegExp from the resolved vkey and matches it anywhere in kmnRules. Vkeys are constrained to K_[A-Z0-9_]+ so there is no metacharacter hazard today, but it over-suppresses in one edge case: if the counterpart is already assigned to the SAME key on a different layer (e.g. base rather than shift), the shift proposal is suppressed even though the parallel slot is empty. P2, benign under propose-then-confirm.
